title.narrative: UNFPA: Social Norm Change and Gender Stereotypes Elimination Ukraine 2024-27
UNFPA: Sociala normförändring och eliminering av könsstereotyper Ukraina 2024-27

description.narrative: Projektet Equality Springboard: Social Norm Change and Gender Stereotypes Elimination syftar till att återställa den sociala strukturen och bygga demografisk motståndskraft i ukrainska samhällen som drabbats av fördrivning och konflikter. Målen är att: - Skapa gynnsamma förutsättningar för social sammanhållning för unga, familjer och individer i riskzonen - Förebygga alla former av våld i hemmet och könsrelaterat våld och psykiska utmaningar För att uppnå detta syftar projektet till att etablera resiliens och social sammanhållning community hubs (REACH) samt att operationalisera och lokalisera nationella strategier mot antidiskriminering och jämställdhet genom införandet av relevant utbildning och mentalt välbefinnande.

The project Equality Springboard: Social Norm Change and Gender Stereotypes Elimination aims to restore social fabric and build demographic resilience in Ukrainian targeted communities affected by displacement and conflict. Objectives are to: - Create favorable conditions for social cohesion of young people, families and individuals at risk - Prevent all forms of domestic and gender-based violence and mental health challenges To achieve this, the project aims to establish resilience and social cohesion community hubs (REACH) as well as to operationalise and localise national strategies toward anti-discrimination and gender equality through the introduction of relevant education and mental well being practices.

The project goal is to strengthen community resilience and prevent gender-based violence by introducing community-led, adaptive, inclusive solutions that promote egalitarian norms and build resilience of youth, women, and men from vulnerable backgrounds in Ukraine.
Project objectives
1) Bolster the psychological and emotional resilience of young people and prevent gender-based violence through the provision of psychological counselling, soft skills training, and comprehensive sexuality education. 2) Promote men engagement and improve psychological resilience within families to mitigate gender-based violence, foster responsible fatherhood through family-focused interventions and provision of targeted psychological support to men and women from vulnerable groups. 3) Integrate SRHR behaviour change communication (BCC) and information education and awareness (IEA) components into the community-run activities aiming to strengthen the resilience of youth, families from vulnerable backgrounds, including families with veterans. 4) Support implementation of gender strategy in education and providing a comprehensive sexuality education framework at the community level to advance egalitarian social norms and prevent gender-based violence.
Expected outcomes
OUTCOME 1. Young people are more psychologically resilient and demonstrate safer behaviours due to improved psychological skills, soft skills, and relationship/sexuality awareness.
Output 1.1. Youth centres are trained to provide resilience-building sessions for youth.
Output 1.2. Young people receive psychological, soft skills and sexuality education training to bolster their resilience skills.
OUTCOME 2. Men, at-risk families and individuals enhance their psychological resilience and embrace egalitarian norms in childcare and family relationships, thereby establishing stronger support networks and preventing gender-based violence within the targeted communities.
Output 2.2. Families, men and women (incl. from vulnerable groups) receive psychological support and participate in sessions to strengthen social cohesion, promote mens engagement in childcare and household support and prevent GBV.
OUTCOME 3. SRHR related knowledge, attitude and practice of young people, families and individuals from vulnerable backgrounds, including veterans, in targeted municipalities is improved through integration of SRHR behaviour change communication (BCC) and information education and counselling (IEC) components into the community-run activities aiming to increase access to SRHR services.
Output 3.1. Community-based initiatives to raise awareness, reduce stigma, and increase access to sexual and reproductive health services.
Output 3.2. Referral paths to Health Care Centers for SRHR services are established.
OUTCOME 4. MoES and education institutions at the local level receive support in implementation of gender strategy in education preventing GBV, and providing a comprehensive sexuality education framework.
Output 4.1. Educators in the targeted communities are sensitised to gender equality, non-discrimination, GBV prevention and psychological resilience.
Output 4.2. MoES and education institutions at the local level receive support in implementation of gender transformative education policies gender strategy in education, comprehensive sexuality education framework).
5 existing tato-hubs and 3 new ones will provide targeted mental health support, GBV prevention and SRHR-awareness for families and men, promoting psychological resilience, responsible fatherhood and addressing toxic masculinity stereotypes.

title.narrative: Beslut om stöd till UNFPA Ukraina 2024-2027
Beslut om stöd till UNFPA Ukraina 2024-2027

description.narrative:
- A total of 66 young women and 14 young men from youth centres and spaces were trained and equipped as peer educators. Through their peer-to-peer activities, they reached a total of 556 girls and 326 boys, supporting their personal development in stress management, mental well-being, gender equality, various soft skills, comprehensive sexuality education, stereotype-free career guidance and financial literacy. This enables them to actively contribute to more resilient and inclusive communities.
- Comprehensive sexuality education was integrated into the national programme for youth centres, managed by the All-Ukrainian Youth Centre. A national pool of 50 peer trainers has been established to sustain efforts and expand reach.
- Through a combination of psychosocial support, educational sessions, and community-based outreach activities, TatoHubs strengthened family resilience, promoted responsible fatherhood, and contributed to the gender-based violence prevention. These efforts reached 11 951 individuals, including 4944 women, 3734 men, 1766 girls and 1507 boys. Notably, 2028 fathers and future fathers, including 135 veterans, enhanced their understanding of non-violent parenting and gender equitable partnerships through engaging in TatoHubs programs. Simultaneously over 1650 women, including pregnant women, as well as 1010 men, 890 boys and girls participated in psychological counseling sessions, reducing emotional tension and anxiety.
- UNFPA strengthened the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, as well as the broader Ukrainian education system by supporting the integration of emotional, ethical and non-discrimination competencies into the revised Professional Teacher´s Standard. The Ministry´s first-ever participatory Gender Audit was also conducted. Following a successful pilot, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine recommended the integration of the Social-Emotional and Ethical Learning programme into the educational framework of the New Ukrainian School model.
- Out of 785 trained educators 691 women and 81 men received certification in professional development programmes at regional conferences on non-discrimination and inclusion in education.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
